Surely one of the greatest assists of all time enabling that last goal. Delivered from one of the greatest players this world will ever know. It’s beautiful to see the Argentinian spirit. 

England’s mistake was to score and then go on the complete defensive. They made that same mistake before.

One of the qualities of Messi is that the more pressure that comes on him the more he rises to majestic and even artistic heights with his craft. I’ve watched the same situations play out in his years with Barcelona. 

Whoever you are behind for winning this tournament, you have to recognize his greatness. It brings me sorrow to know that one day he will not be on the field anymore. We were also lucky to see him in our lifetime. 

This is great flames come up in humanity once every two or 300 years. You have people like Bob Dylan who changed the face of songwriting in the West forever. There are many others like this great and small. Messi is definitely one of the great flames to burn so brightly ❤

comment_text: Its incredible to think that Zverev played at the highest possible level. He went out of his comfort zone , took risks , served brilliantly, went for winners instead of dragging the rallies. But still couldn't even break Sinners serve. Zverev came out with a fantastic gameplan and played lights out tennis. Sinner was also surprised with Zverevs level and took little more time than usual to figure him out. In the process Zverev won the 1st set tiebreaker. Second set onwards,  Sinner started to read the serve well, returned much better and deep and overall raised his level. As a result Zverev started fading when Sinner figured him out and got checkmate. It was a memorable final kind of a chess match.. but the bottomline is - Even Zverev's best level is not enough to beat Sinner...

comment_text:
Mirra Andreeva , I have been following this kid for three years. Even though Elena Rybakina is still my favorite player, I always felt that Mirra had the potential to become one of the future faces of tennis. Because of all the controversy and criticism surrounding Russian players, I really wanted her to prove her doubters wrong on the court.
After Elena's upset exit, I started hoping that Mirra would go all the way and lift her maiden Grand Slam trophy. Following World No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka's exit, she became one of the favorites for the title.
In the semifinals, she faced Marta Kostyuk in a match that carried plenty of political baggage, but Mirra stayed focused and got her revenge for Madrid. She then defeated the talented Polish player Maja Chwalińska, bringing her fairytale run to an end.
And now Mirra has done it—she has won her maiden Roland Garros title. What an incredible achievement for such a young player.
There were thousands of comments spreading this kind of NATO propaganda and nonsense. Why should players be held responsible for a war they have nothing to do with? Tennis players are athletes, not politicians. I'm glad Mirra answered her critics the best way possible—with her performances on the court and by winning.


P.S. Elena Rybakina will always be my favorite player, and I'll support her forever. But after Lena's early exit, I'm genuinely happy that Mirra went on to win the tournament. ❤🏆
